Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: NIDA provides digital authentication via the Common Interface Gateway (CIG) and APIs: fingerprint/PIN matching against the central database, NFC contactless smartcard authentication, PKI for online services, and USSD-based NIN retrieval. Financial institutions, telecoms, and government agencies use NIDA APIs for real-time biometric eKYC.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: The NIDA National ID (NIN) is required to access e-government platforms, including BRELA Online Registration System (business registration), RITA e-Huduma (civil registration), e-government portals, and the Tanzania e-Passport application. The NIN enables access to government digital services including social protection programs (TASAF) and health insurance (NHIF).

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Individuals can access their NIN and ID data via NIDA Online Portal (services.nida.go.tz), USSD (*152*00# via Vodacom/Airtel), or NIDA offices. The portal allows citizens to retrieve their NIN, view ID details, and generate payment control numbers. The PDPA 2022 also grants data subjects rights to access, correct, and request erasure of personal data.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: NIDA NIN and biometric database are used for eKYC across banking, financial services, and telecoms. The Bank of Tanzania and AMLA require NIN-based KYC for account opening. NIDA integrates with 124+ institutions via CIG/APIs. KYC platforms (VOVE ID, Youverify, uqudo) use NIDA integration for real-time identity verification.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: NIDA is partially integrated with civil registration. NIDA is fully integrated with Zanzibar's civil registry. On Tanzania mainland, RITA (Registration, Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency) has been digitizing and integrating with NIDA; the 2024 National Financial Inclusion Report and ID4Africa 2025 note ongoing NIDA-RITA integration. However, NIDA-RITA interoperability was still described as partial/in-progress with only 2 of 17 envisaged integrations complete as of recent assessments.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: NIDA shares data via Data Sharing Agreements (DSAs) with public and private entities (45 signed, 22 pending by 2021; expanded to 124+ institutions by 2025). Fees charged per query. The PDPA 2022 (in force 2023) partially regulates data sharing. However, DSA terms are not publicly disclosed and no requirement for individual consent or notification. Rules exist but are only partially publicly available.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Tanzania has specific digital ID legislation: RIPA No. 11 of 1986 and its 2014 Regulations explicitly govern the NIDA national digital ID system. The 2023 Biometrics update and 2025 plans to enact the Infant Registration Bill further confirm specific digital ID regulatory framework. The Electronic Transactions Act (Cap. 442) and 2025 Digital Certification Services Regulations also apply.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: The Personal Data Protection Act No. 11 of 2022 was passed by Tanzania's National Assembly on 27 November 2022 and came into force on 1 May 2023. It establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission and regulates collection, processing and sharing of personal data.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (in force May 2023) established the Personal Data Protection Commission as the supervisory authority responsible for enforcement and compliance, including registration of data controllers and processors. Final registration deadline for entities was 30 April 2025.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The NIDA National ID card serves as the primary legal proof of identity in Tanzania and is required for passports, SIM registration, bank account opening, government employment, TIN, and other services. Under RIPA and 2014 Regulations, it is the authoritative identity document. NIDA was designated the sole data controller under the 2019/2021 Written Laws Amendments.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: The NIDA system is governed by the Registration and Identification of Persons Act (RIPA) No. 11 of 1986 (enforced 2011), its 2014 Regulations, and the Registration of Zanzibaris Residents Act (RZRA) No. 7 of 2005. Written Laws (Miscellaneous Amendments) Acts 2019 and 2021 designated NIDA as sole data controller. The Personal Data Protection Act 2022 came into force May 2023.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: The initial feasibility study was conducted by Gotham International (UK) in 2006. Ongoing system maintenance involves mixed in-country and foreign vendor involvement. NIDA runs its own data center and district offices, but ICT infrastructure upgrades (e.g., Tanzania Digital Project) involve external technical partners. Full in-country control not confirmed.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: NIDA falls under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MoHA), not the Ministry of Finance. However, NIDA's budget is appropriated annually through Parliament and the MoF has general budgetary oversight of all government agencies. The NAO audit (2020) confirmed MoHA oversight of NIDA's finances. Ministry of Finance exercises partial oversight through the national budget process.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: NIDA has moved toward financial self-sustainability by charging fees for identity verification ($0.18 per transaction), card replacement, and legal resident registration, generating approximately $45.4 million from verification services. However, the Tanzania Digital Project upgrade still relies on World Bank/IDA support. Budget allocations for 2025/26 (5.81bn/- for registrations) come from government, while infrastructure modernization is donor-assisted.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: NIDA collects fingerprints (via AFIS - Automated Fingerprint Identification System) as primary biometric, plus facial photo during biometric registration. The smart card stores biometric credentials. The 2025 infant biometric pilot also uses facial data. Baker McKenzie confirms biometric registration includes fingerprinting and photo.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: NIDA operates a fully digital centralized database stored in an ISO 27001/ISO 9001-certified data center connected to all district offices via the national ICT broadband backbone. The NFC smart card (80kb contactless) stores digital biometric credentials. All registration data is digitally processed and stored.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Tanzania operates a fully deployed nationwide digital ID system managed by the National Identification Authority (NIDA), established under the Registration and Identification of Persons Act (RIPA). As of December 2024, NIDA has registered 25,484,820 individuals and issued over 20 million National ID cards nationwide.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: NIDA has integrated with over 124 institutions (public and private) via Common Interface Gateway (CIG) and APIs. Systems interconnected include RITA (civil registration), TRA (tax), BRELA (business registration), NHIF, TASAF, social security schemes, and TIRA. E-government authority data platform also links multiple MDAs.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The NIDA NIN is mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing banking services under Bank of Tanzania regulations. NIDA integration enables real-time eKYC for banks and fintechs. The 2024 Annual Financial Inclusion Report confirms NIN/cards are 'crucial in opening bank accounts and accessing banking services'.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The first-time issuance of the NIDA national ID card is free to citizens and eligible residents. Replacement or correction requests incur fees (payment control numbers generated via NIDA Online Portal). The initial registration and first card issuance carry no cost to the applicant.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Some EAC nationals (Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda) can use their national IDs for cross-border travel within the EAC, but Tanzania's NIDA National ID card is not formally listed as accepted for travel by other EAC states. Tanzania uses the EAC e-Passport (launched January 2018) for formal regional travel. Some regional acceptance exists but formal interoperability of the NIDA ID specifically across borders is limited.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Under current law (RIPA 1986 and 2014 Regulations), enrollment eligibility is 18 years and above. The Infant Registration Bill (to be tabled in Parliament) would extend NIDA registration to newborns via the Jamii Namba initiative, but as of early 2026 this has not yet been enacted. Pilot programs for under-18 registration are planned but not yet in force.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Enrollment is mandatory for all eligible Tanzanians. RIPA Section 20 makes it an offence to refuse or fail to comply with registration requirements. The 2014 Regulations use 'shall' and require registration within 90 days of reaching 18. Mandatory use is reinforced through exclusive NIDA ID requirements for passports, SIM registration, bank accounts, TIN, and government employment.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: NIDA NIN is integrated with the National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) and the Universal Health Coverage (UHC) Act 2023 requires NIN-linked enrollment. TASAF beneficiaries are being integrated into the UHC system via NIDA. The NIN is accepted (not yet universally mandatory) for healthcare access. The UHC Act mandates health insurance enrollment for all Tanzanians linked to NIN.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: NIDA registers legal residents (with valid permits), refugees (using refugee ID/ration card), and certain aliens. Diplomats are exempt from fingerprint requirements. Stateless persons living in Tanzania are also eligible. Not all non-nationals qualify — tourists and irregular migrants are excluded. The system allows 'some' non-nationals (legal residents, refugees) but not all.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: As of April 2025, NIDA registered 25.8 million individuals, representing 81.9% of the 31,582,976 people aged 18 and above per the 2022 census. Of Tanzania's total population of ~64.2 million (including under-18s), coverage is approximately 43%. The eligible adult population (18+) coverage is ~82%, placing this in the 70-89% bracket for the eligible population.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: Independent security reviews have been conducted on NIDA. The National Audit Office (NAO) conducted a Performance Audit on NIDA in 2020/2021. NIDA's data center is certified to ISO 27001 (information security management) and ISO 9001 (quality management) standards. The RIA (Research ICT Africa) conducted an independent rights-based assessment in 2021. These constitute external security/performance reviews.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration using NIDA NIN and biometrics is mandatory in Tanzania. The TCRA mandated NIDA-only SIM registration with deadline enforced by May 2019. Using an unregistered SIM is an offence under the Electronic and Postal Communications Act (Section 131). The Fahamu Namba ya NIDA mandate explicitly requires NIN for SIM activation.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: NIDA ID is accepted for and integrated with social services. NIDA is integrated with TASAF (Tanzania Social Action Fund) for cash transfers and social protection programs. The National Social Protection Policy 2023 and 2024 Financial Inclusion Report confirm NIDA integration with social security schemes. However, social services access is not universally mandatory via NIDA ID alone.
